scope: Root token cleanup through the current Oop API

contract_review.operation_sequence: releaseTokensProtecting(result, tokens...) -> validate all token representations -> current release: sends in reverse order -> report first failure after attempting all releases; unchanged
contract_review.ownership: Roots continues to own token inventory; Id retains only its normal entered-call references. The test uses public messages and a declared C observer.

retained_checks: Tokens are distinct and monotonically allocated; repeated object roots preserve registry observations
Successful cleanup leaves the same watched root order as ordinary reverse release
Malformed token input rejects before any token is released; empty cleanup is invalid and result-only cleanup succeeds
A release callback replaces release:; every later token enters the replacement
Collecting release callbacks complete cleanup on success, duplicate/absent tokens and multiple exact native failures
The first native failure wins while every later release is attempted
Retired raw-byte retain/release batching APIs remain absent
adaptation_note: The removed tryReleaseMany: shortcut had a different failure contract. Current releaseTokensProtecting reports duplicate/absent-token failure and temporarily roots its first failure while continuing. That temporary root can change swap-removal enumeration order. The final test requires exact successful inventory order, exact reverse callback order on both success and failure, and complete draining on failure; it does not require the error path inventory to match a loop without error protection.

development_probe.observation: An initial comparison exposed different remaining-root enumeration order after a duplicate/absent-token error, due to temporary first-failure protection. No runtime change was made.

limits: Staged-prefix component checks, not full integration qualification
Method construction purity and closure admission regressions remain open
root_reuse and other legacy harnesses remain unported
